faithful_fixed_module_prefix_ranks.scope: One fixed univariate module per actual commuting quotient, with query shifts from exact chain lengths. This is faithful for special and nonreduced samples, and is not the generic min(n,carrier-rank) formula.

uniform_results.rank: R(n,M,S)=sum_u min(q,l_u)+R(r,M/p,{u:l_u>q}), n=q*(M/p)+r, M a power of p >= n
uniform_results.homogeneous_subset_enumerator: H(n,M,A,B,Y)=H(r,M/p,A_prime,B_prime,Y), with the two explicit binomial sums in (O16)
uniform_results.code_weight_enumerator: W_C(z)=H(n,M,1-z,Q*z,1/Q) for C=<(V-1)^n> over a finite field of size Q and characteristic p
uniform_results.division_free_circuit: O(p*s+log(M+1)) integer-constant arithmetic gates for the complete enumerator, M=p^s; coefficient expansion and integer bit costs are additional

prime_digit_rank_law.scope: Exact rank, minimum-cost basis, subset-rank and code-weight recursions for the truncated Pascal matrix over prime characteristic. Independent controls use arbitrary column subsets, actual unit-power quotients and polynomial-generated codewords. This is repeated-root cyclic-code structure; strongest priority and the comparison with existing weight-distribution algorithms remain open. No novelty, coherent-fan lower bound or improvement of unrestricted G3 is asserted.

direct_positive_cone_traversal.scope: Complete positive-cone traversal independently compared with exhaustive monomial-basis polytopes, the older full reconstruction and direct ground elimination. The checker uses elementary field arithmetic; fast-field bounds rely on the cited Neiger--Schost backend.

shifted_module_profile_obstruction.uniform_scope: The cyclic-span rank polytope and the fixed K[T]-quotient invariant factors do not preserve the positive fan. The exact missing information is the classical aggregated matroid valuation, whose quadratic contact set is the feasible prefix set. The moment-graph family realizes the existing corner-cut class; it gives no supergeneric lower bound.

uniform_results.geometric_operations: O((g+1)*n^(5/3)*L) exact integer/rational operations and cost comparisons via direct positive-cone traversal
uniform_results.unrestricted_shadow_geometric_consequenc: O(n^(109/24)*L^(11/8)) rational geometric operations and comparisons
uniform_results.combined_unit_cost_consequence: O(n^(omega+23/8)*L^(11/8)) field and geometric arithmetic operations combined, plus one-time preprocessing already dominated asymptotically; not a coefficient-bit bound
uniform_results.classical_count_composition: O(n^(omega+3)*L) field operations, plus one-time O(n^3*L^2) preprocessing
uniform_results.given_input: One marked reduced Groebner basis, or commuting coordinate matrices with a cyclic vector.
uniform_results.union_output: All reduced bases; their union may retain repeated polynomials.

scope: Neiger--Schost Theorem 1.7 and Proposition 3.7 apply to arbitrary commuting matrices and monomial orders. Direct positive-cone traversal, using classical Groebner cone descriptions and adjacency, is independently compared with exhaustive state polytopes and the retained older oracle reconstruction. Exact polar hulls remove the previous quadratic output geometry budget. Field arithmetic in this checker is elementary; the theorem uses published fast linear algebra. No new general traversal method, unrestricted count, current-best priority, coefficient-bit cost or practical speedup is established.
